text: Definite strong vibes of Elliott Smith and Daniel Johnson coming from this one. Gentle and vulnerable but there is a strength to his simple songwriting that is the real deal and feels very unaffected. Be very interesting to see where he goes next.

Feels potentially more life-wrecked than his PA contemporary Alexander Giannascoli (who more often taps into a shared frequency, like the kids in the two Schoenbrun movies he scored). This kind of songwriting is an established idiom, but it says something that we can't come up with so many prime examples of it—it's hard to dependably hit that sore spot, not lapse into fake emotion, and Mendez hits it square on a bunch of times on a short record.

With obvious inspirations from two of my favorite artists, Elliot Smith and Alex G, I'm bound to like him. Sweet and soft, this album is a great slowcore acoustic (for the most part) album. His lyrics are personal and touching and overall I have a lot of love for this album. Of course, I love Maria. It sounds like one of Alex Gs old acoustic unreleased demos with the strumming pattern of the guitar and the lyrics.

There's so much pressure to be "novel," these days; everything always has to be "boundary pushing" to get any indie cred. Greg Mendez, though, manages to be "novel" simply by wearing his influences on his sleeve. Elliott Smith, Sufjan Stevens—the names are almost cliché at this point, and yet these are Mendez's touchstones. It's simple music, yes. But so pure. Pitchfork says this album will "restore your faith in squeaky acoustic guitar, whispery vocals, and confessional lyrics." For me, my music taste started with this kind of "acoustic guitar shit": and then, like the rest of us, I got jaded; I thought I had moved past it. Greg Mendez gives me the OK to return to my roots and to feel warmed at its hearth.

i had not listened to greg mendez before this album, as is seemingly the case for most people outside of philly, but i've been very glad that i did. he hews close to elliott smith in sound in many respects but it's not like a 1-to-1 copy either. he just has an incredibly good voice and some songwriting skills to back it up. the run of tracks 3-7 is truly fucking incredible and the other 4 songs are still good even if it's hard for me to ever remember them. goodbye / trouble is one of the best songs that you will hear on any album this year if you have any love in your heart for singer-songwriter type music.

Extremely promising. Some songs feel a little underdeveloped and end prematurely, but the foundations of an excellent singer songwriter are all here. The last 3 are particular bops and point the direction that Greg can go in. I will be excited to see what he does next.
